definitions.explanation: A keigo (honorific language) term meaning to receive something, used to show deep respect toward the giver. It lowers oneself to elevate the person who gave or sent the item.

examples.japanese: お⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧{拝受|はいじゅ}⟦いたしました→いたす：01314_itasu⟧。
⟦{資料|しりょう}→資料：04166_shiryou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{拝受|はいじゅ}⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、ご⟦{報告|ほうこく}→報告：03618_houkoku⟧⟦いたします→いたす：01314_itasu⟧。
examples.english: I am reporting that I have received the documents.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先日|せんじつ}→先日：03305_senjitsu⟧お⟦{送|おく}り→送る：00742_okuru⟧⟦いただいた→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧お⟦{品物|しなもの}→品物：00886_shinamono⟧、⟦{確|たし}か→確か：00894_tashika⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{拝受|はいじゅ}⟦いたしました→いたす：01314_itasu⟧。
examples.english: I can confirm that I have received the item you kindly sent the other day.

notes:
A humble (kenjoogo) expression for receiving something. It is the humble counterpart of ⟦{受|う}け{取|と}る→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧ and is considerably more formal. Used primarily in written correspondence, especially business emails and formal letters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拝受|はいじゅ}⟦いたしました→いたす：01314_itasu⟧: I have (humbly) received
- {拝受|はいじゅ}⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧: I have received (slightly less formal)
- お⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧{拝受|はいじゅ}: receipt of your letter
- ⟦{確|たし}か→確か：00894_tashika⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{拝受|はいじゅ}: confirmed receipt

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{受領|じゅりょう}→受領：20050_juryou⟧: receipt — formal but not humble; used in official/administrative contexts
- ⟦{受|う}け{取|と}る→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧: to receive — neutral, everyday term
- ⟦{頂戴|ちょうだい}する→頂戴する：05913_choudaisuru⟧: to receive (humble) — less formal than {拝受|はいじゅ}, also used in speech
- ⟦{賜|たまわ}る→賜る：07659_tamawaru⟧: to be granted (humble/respectful) — used when receiving from someone of very high status

REGISTER:
This is one of the most formal ways to say 'I received.' It appears almost exclusively in written Japanese, particularly in business email and official correspondence. In spoken Japanese, {頂|いただ}きました or ⟦{受|う}け{取|と}りました→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧ are preferred.
